name: Silver dapple
summary: Silver (PMEL, formerly PMEL17 or SILV), a dominant dilution of black pigment caused by one missense change in exon 11 of the gene (Arg618Cys). It lightens black toward chocolate on the body and toward flaxen or silver-grey on the mane and tail, and leaves red pigment alone: a black becomes chocolate with a pale mane, a bay keeps its red body and its black points turn silver, and a chestnut carrying it looks unchanged while still passing it on. The same variant causes multiple congenital ocular anomalies (MCOA), an eye disorder that is milder with one copy and severe with two. Also called silver dapple, taffy or chocolate.

phenotypes.name: Silver dapple
phenotypes.description: Black pigment walked toward chocolate, and most of the way to flaxen on the mane and tail, with red untouched - a chocolate body under a pale mane on a black horse, silver bay on a bay. A chestnut carrier looks unchanged.

conditions.name: Ocular cysts (MCOA, one copy)
conditions.description: One silver copy. The milder form of multiple congenital ocular anomalies: translucent cysts of the iris, the ciliary body or the retina, often with few or no clinical signs. It is present whether or not the coat shows silver.

conditions.name: Multiple congenital ocular anomalies
conditions.description: Two silver copies. The severe form: an enlarged cornea, an abnormal iris or retina and cataracts, with sight impaired and sometimes lost.
